Fig. 13. Visualization of feature maps in our MRFE module. We showcase outputs from different branches within MRFE. The identity mapping branch retains original features; the 5× 5 kernel branch emphasizes local texture details, while the 11× 11 and 17× 17 kernel branches focus more on capturing global contextual structures. This demonstrates the effectiveness of MRFE in modeling both fine-grained and large-scale spatial information.

Fig. 6. Visual comparison of pixel-wise error maps on the Urban100 (×4) dataset. The GT is provided to illustrate the complex high-frequency structures; the consistently minimal residuals (darker regions) produced by EchoSR demonstrate its superior structural fidelity and absence of texture hallucinations.

TABLE XIII QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS ON THE ERF WITH THE HIGH-CONTRIBUTION AREA RATIO FOR VARIOUS KERNEL CONFIGURATIONS OF THE COFB MODULE. THE AREA IS MEASURED AS THE PERCENTAGE OF SPATIAL REGIONS REQUIRED TO COVER SPECIFIC CUMULATIVE CONTRIBUTION SCORE THRESHOLDS, FOR INSTANCE, A VALUE OF 20.7305% AT THE 70% THRESHOLD INDICATES THAT 20.7305% OF PIXELS ACCOUNT FOR 70% OF THE TOTAL CONTRIBUTION SCORES.

Fig. 17. Quantitative analysis of ERF area ratio relative change across various cumulative contribution score thresholds (10%–95%). The curves depict the percentage change between “before” and “after” COFB states. The proposed 7 → 15 cascaded sequence in COFB achieves a stable and constructive expansion of the receptive field. In contrast, the reversed 15 → 7 sequence and single-kernel baselines exhibit significant contraction and structural dissipation in critical core regions.
